topic.name: ALK
topic.short_description: Fusion gene target in non-small cell lung cancer
topic.seo_title: ALK Fusion Gene in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer - Latest Research & Diagnostics | Your Cancer Breakthroughs
topic.seo_description: Discover ALK fusion gene testing and targeted therapies for non-small cell lung cancer. Explore latest biomarker research, diagnostic advances, and treatment breakthroughs.
topic.seo_intro:
ALK (anaplastic lymphoma kinase) fusion genes represent an important biomarker in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that has transformed how doctors diagnose and treat certain patients. When the ALK gene fuses with other genes, it can drive cancer cell growth, making it a prime target for specialized therapies. Approximately 3-5% of NSCLC patients have ALK-positive tumors, and identifying this genetic alteration through advanced diagnostic testing has become a critical component of precision cancer care.

The discovery of ALK as a therapeutic target has led to the development of ALK inhibitors—medications specifically designed to block the protein produced by this fusion gene. This targeted approach has significantly improved outcomes for ALK-positive patients compared to traditional chemotherapy alone. Ongoing research continues to explore new ALK inhibitors, strategies to overcome drug resistance, and how ALK testing can be integrated into standard diagnostic protocols to ensure all eligible patients benefit from these advances.

On this page, you'll find the latest peer-reviewed studies and clinical research focused on ALK as a biomarker and diagnostic tool in lung cancer. These articles represent current scientific evidence to help patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers understand the importance of ALK testing and emerging treatment options in precision oncology.

articles.title: A Phase I, Open-Label, Multicenter, Dose Escalation and Cohort Expansion Study of AQUA07 Monotherapy and Combination Therapy in Patients With Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase-Positive Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
articles.hook: AQUA07 combined with lorlatinib shows activity in ALK-positive lung cancer
articles.summary: Researchers are testing AQUA07, a new drug alone and combined with lorlatinib, to treat ALK-positive lung cancer.

articles.title: Alectinib and gastrointestinal perforation in ALK-rearranged non-small cell lung cancer: A case series.
articles.hook: Alectinib causes gastrointestinal perforation in ALK-positive lung cancer patients
articles.summary: Alectinib, a lung cancer drug, rarely causes life-threatening stomach perforation in some patients.

articles.title: Design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of BODIPY-based photoactivatable Crizotinib prodrugs for precision cancer therapy.
articles.hook: BODIPY-based photoactivatable Crizotinib prodrugs target ALK-positive lung cancer
articles.summary: Researchers developed light-activated Crizotinib prodrugs using BODIPY technology to reduce toxicity and improve precision treatment of ALK-positive lung cancer.

articles.title: Transformation of ALK-translocated lung adenocarcinoma to LCNEC under alectinib treatment-a case report and mini-review.
articles.hook: Alectinib treatment triggers transformation to neuroendocrine lung cancer in ALK-positive patient
articles.summary: ALK-positive lung cancer transformed into a more aggressive neuroendocrine type during treatment with alectinib, revealing a rare resistance mechanism.

articles.title: Discovery of novel anaplastic lymphoma kinase inhibitors with enhanced binding interactions for non-small cell lung cancer via in silico approaches and retrospective experimental data support.
articles.hook: Five novel ALK inhibitors show comparable efficacy to current treatments in lung cancer
articles.summary: Researchers identified five new drug candidates that inhibit ALK protein in lung cancer, with one showing effectiveness comparable to current treatments.

articles.title: Repurposing ALK Inhibitors as Influenza and Corona Virus Antivirals Targeting Lymphocyte Tyrosine Kinase (LTK).
articles.hook: ALK inhibitors target lymphocyte tyrosine kinase to inhibit influenza and COVID-19
articles.summary: Existing cancer drugs that inhibit ALK show promise as antivirals against influenza and COVID-19 by targeting a host cell protein viruses need.

articles.title: [Autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis induced by brigatinib: a case report and literature review].
articles.hook: Brigatinib induces autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis in lung cancer patients
articles.summary: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors can cause a rare lung disease (autoimmune PAP) treatable with GM-CSF or lung lavage.

articles.title: MATCH Treatment Subprotocol C2: Crizotinib in Patients With Tumors With MET Exon 14 Deletion
articles.hook: Crizotinib targets MET exon 14 deletion tumors in MATCH trial
articles.summary: Crizotinib targets tumors with MET exon 14 deletion mutations by blocking growth-promoting enzymes in cancer cells.

articles.title: A Phase I/Ib Dose Escalation and Biomarker Study of Ceritinib (LDK378) in Combination With Everolimus in Patients With Locally Advanced or Metastatic Solid Tumors With an Expansion in NSCLC Characterized by Abnormalities in Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase (ALK) Expression
articles.hook: Ceritinib plus everolimus combination targets ALK-positive advanced lung cancer
articles.summary: Ceritinib combined with everolimus shows promise as a treatment for advanced lung cancer with ALK mutations.

articles.title: Phase I Study of Ceritinib Plus Docetaxel in ALK-Negative, EGFR WT Advanced NSCLC
articles.hook: Ceritinib plus docetaxel combination establishes safety in advanced lung cancer
articles.summary: A Phase I study testing ceritinib and docetaxel combination therapy to find the safe dose and effectiveness in advanced lung cancer patients.
